import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A Brightwater maintenance ticket names the item it is about; a booking line
names the piece of equipment it rents. Documents point at other documents. A
`reference` field holds one typed link, a collection reference holds many,
and a long text field can carry links inside markdown. Facet indexes every
link, so each document page can also show the reverse: which documents point
here.

## When to use this

Use reference fields when one record names another record but does not own
it — a ticket names its item, a booking names its client. When the part
belongs to the whole, model composition instead (see
[Parent and child documents](/build/model/relations/parent-child/)).

## Before you start

- **A qualified target.** The target of a reference is always a qualified
  doctype id: `domain.Doctype`, for example `equipment.Item`. Facet rejects a
  bare name when you save the doctype, so a dead field never reaches your
  data.
- **Read access to the target.** Users need read access to a target doctype
  to resolve its references.
- **Where the target lives.** A reference can point into another domain —
  see [Share data across domains](/build/model/relations/across-domains/)
  for the rules that apply between domains.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the doctype in the **Builder** and add a field of type
   **Reference**.
2. Pick the target doctype. The editor qualifies the target while you work in
   a draft — you may see the draft's own id as the prefix. On publish, Facet
   relinks every same-domain target to the published domain name, so the
   stored form is always the live one.
3. Optionally set a **Filter** to restrain the picker.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

The Brightwater maintenance ticket declares its item reference:

```yaml
# equipment/doctypes/equipment.MaintenanceTicket.yml (extract)
fields:
  item:
    type: reference
    title: Item
    doctype: equipment.Item
    required: true
    filters: [equality]
```

The target is the qualified form `equipment.Item` — a bare `Item` is
rejected.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### What writers may submit

Users and API callers can send a bare id, a qualified id, or a `urn:facet:`
token. Facet stores the qualified form in every case:

| You send | Facet stores |
| --- | --- |
| `EQ-2026-0001` | `equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001` |
| `equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001` | `equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001` |
| `urn:facet:equipment:Item:EQ-2026-0001` | `equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001` |

### Restrain the picker with a filter

The optional `filter` limits which documents a reference accepts. Facet
checks the filter on every write:

```json
"company": {
  "type": "reference",
  "doctype": "clients.Company",
  "filter": { "status__eq": "active" }
}
```

### Allow forward references

A reference normally must point at a document that exists. Set
`dangling: true` when the target may not exist yet, for example a successor
filled in a later step.

### Point at many documents

Add `collection: true` to hold an array of references. Facet checks each
element in turn, and rejects a list that names the same target twice:

```json
"watchers": {
  "type": "reference",
  "doctype": "iam.Account",
  "collection": true
}
```

### Link inside long text

A `longtext` field accepts markdown links to documents. Both forms below
produce a link on the page and count as a link in the index:

```markdown
Checked with [Nadia](urn:facet:iam:Account:nadia@brightwater.example).

Follow-up for [Main tent 10x15](equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001).
```

Both forms count: a `urn:facet:` token anywhere in the text, and a markdown
link whose address is a document. A dotted address typed in plain prose,
without a link, does not count.

## Example

Three Brightwater references, each pointing at a different kind of target:

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "item": { "type": "reference", "doctype": "equipment.Item", "required": true, "filters": ["equality"] },
    "assignee": { "type": "reference", "doctype": "iam.Account", "filters": ["equality"] },
    "client": { "type": "reference", "doctype": "clients.Company", "required": true, "filters": ["equality"] }
  }
}
```

On each document page, the **Referenced by** section lists the documents that
point here. Before a delete, Facet warns:
`N document(s) reference it — deleting it leaves those links dangling`. The
delete is never blocked; the warning is there to inform the choice.

## Troubleshooting

### The doctype refuses to save with a target error

The declared `doctype` must be the qualified form `domain.Doctype`. A bare
name such as `"Item"` fails at definition time, before any value is written.

### A write answers `422` with a doctype error

The referenced doctype is not registered — most often because it still lives
only in a draft. Publish the draft first, then write the reference.

### A reference shows as empty or not found

The target document was deleted, or your role cannot read its doctype. Facet
keeps the stored value but resolves nothing for you.
